metaTitle: Best Microwave Air Fryer Combos in 2026
metaDescription: Six countertop microwave and air fryer combos compared on wattage, cavity size, convection design, sensors and how well each crisps food.
expertTake: The Toshiba OptiChef Pro Max 1.3 cu ft is the best combo because it pairs 1100 watts with a top fan that mimics an air fryer oven and an inverter. The Ninja Crispi MW101 is the pick for the strongest air frying. Skip combos if you only want a fast microwave, since a plain model heats faster and costs less.
introParagraphs: A microwave air fryer combo folds two countertop appliances into one body. A magnetron heats food from the inside, while a convection fan and heating element crisp the surface, and the better machines can chain both in one program.

These units are compromises by nature. They save counter space and add convenience, yet the air frying is usually gentler than a dedicated basket, so the real question is how much crisp you need and how much room you have.

products.name: Toshiba OptiChef Pro Max 1.3 cu ft, 1100W

specList.label: Air fry system
specList.value: ChefFry Plus top fan and element

specList.label: Best for
specList.value: Households replacing a microwave and an air fryer

products.description:
Toshiba builds the OptiChef Pro Max around a 1.3 cubic foot cavity, 1100 watts of microwave power and a 2.4 inch colour screen. ChefFry Plus adds a top fan and heating element that replicate an air fryer oven, and an inverter and humidity sensor round out the microwave side.

The inverter delivers continuous power rather than on-off pulses, which helps with gentle defrosting and reheating. The top-mounted fan and element are what give the combo a real crisping mode. Compared with the Sharp, it has a larger cavity and more power, and compared with the Ninja it gives up some air fry strength.

The color screen makes the menus easy to follow. Keep the turntable and the crisping tray clean, since splatter bakes on under the element. Measure the counter and the vent clearance before ordering. Year-two issues on any combo tend to be the door latch and the turntable motor, so avoid slamming the door and keep the roller ring clean.
products.bestFor: Households that want a strong microwave and a capable crisping mode in one body.
pros: ChefFry Plus top fan and element
cons: Air frying is gentler than a dedicated basket
Large cavity needs generous counter space

products.name: Ninja Crispi MW101 microwave and air fryer, FusionCrisp
products.description:
Ninja positions the MW101 as a replacement for both a countertop microwave and an air fryer. FusionCrisp starts with microwaving and finishes with air frying, and the listing quotes the power and performance of a 1700 watt Ninja air fryer, up to 450F.

Microwave-then-crisp is the useful idea: it cooks the middle fast and then browns the outside, which suits frozen pizza, chicken pieces and leftovers. Compared with the Toshiba, it leans harder into air frying and less into the microwave side. It is the pick when crisping is the main reason you are buying.

A bigger convection system means more to clean and a hotter body. Wipe splatter after each use and leave generous clearance. Check the microwave wattage in the manual before relying on package times. Place food on the supplied crisping tray for the air fry stage, and keep it clear of the walls so the airflow can reach the underside.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want true air fry power inside a microwave.
cons: Heavy and hot compared with a plain microwave

products.name: Panasonic HomeChef 4-in-1, 1000W, 20 presets
products.description:
Panasonic's HomeChef is a 4-in-1 with 1000 watts, a 1.2 cubic foot cavity and twenty presets. App-linked recipes from the Panasonic Kitchen+ app guide you through dishes and send the settings to the oven.

The guided recipe idea suits cooks who are new to combo ovens and want help with times and sequences. The hardware is solid but less aggressive than the Ninja on crisping. Against the Toshiba, it has fewer cooking extras and more handholding.

App features depend on keeping a phone and account in play, so confirm the physical controls cover the basics. Wipe the cavity after each use. Check ventilation space around the unit. A phone-linked appliance is only as useful as the app is maintained, so look at how recently the app has been updated before you commit.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want app-guided recipes and a 1000W microwave.
pros: 1.2 cu ft cavity fits a dinner plate
cons: App support depends on software upkeep
Crisping is less aggressive than the Ninja

products.name: Sharp SMC0985KS 3-in-1 convection air fry, 900W

specList.label: Multi-stage
specList.value: Up to three stages in one run

products.description:
Sharp makes the SMC0985KS a compact 3-in-1 with 900 watts, a 0.9 cubic foot cavity and multi-stage cooking of up to three functions in one run. Preset buttons and a plus-thirty key handle common tasks.

Multi-stage cooking lets you defrost, cook and crisp without touching the controls in between. Its size suits a small kitchen or a dorm, though 900 watts is on the slower side of the microwave sweet spot. Compared with the Toshiba, it is smaller and cheaper, and it gives up power and capacity.

Expect longer microwave times than a 1100 watt model, and adjust package instructions. Clean the interior regularly to prevent odours. A compact body is easier to place but tighter for large plates. Test a dinner plate in the cavity on the first day, since a turntable that clips the walls will stop turning and heat unevenly.
products.bestFor: Small kitchens that need a compact combo.
cons: Small cavity struggles with big plates

products.name: BLACK+DECKER 5-in-1 microwave air fryer, 0.9 cu ft, 900W

specList.label: Functions
specList.value: Microwave, air fry, convection bake and roast

specList.label: Best for
specList.value: Budget combos with air fry presets

products.description:
BLACK+DECKER's compact 5-in-1 has 900 watts across ten power levels, seven auto menus and eleven air fry presets. Convection bake and roast round out the function list.

The eleven air fry presets are the standout, since they take guesswork out of fries, nuggets and wings in a machine that is new to many owners. It is the budget route into a combo and the compact size fits tight counters. Against the Sharp, it adds more presets, and against the Toshiba it has less power and a smaller cavity.

Small cavities mean small portions, so test your usual plate. Wipe splatter after each use. Keep the vent clear. Remember that air fry presets are written for typical portions, so a half load may finish early and a full load may need extra minutes.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who want many air fry presets.

products.name: Toshiba 8-in-1 air fryer combo microwave, 1.0 cu ft

specList.label: Functions
specList.value: Microwave, air fry, convection bake, broil

products.description:
Toshiba's 8-in-1 combines microwave, air fry, convection bake and broil in a 1.0 cubic foot body with a 12.4 inch turntable that fits a dinner plate. Pro Defrost and a two-step child lock round out the feature set.

A broil element is a rare extra on a combo and lets you melt cheese or finish a crust. The two-step child lock is a genuine plus in a family kitchen. Against the OptiChef Pro Max, it is a size smaller with a simpler interface.

The broil and convection sections need regular wiping to avoid smoke. Check the manual for which accessories are safe in each mode. Leave clearance on all sides. Pro Defrost is a gentler programme than a plain power-level defrost, but meat still needs turning and resting afterwards to even out cold spots.
products.bestFor: Families who want a child lock and a broil element.
pros: 12.4 inch turntable fits a dinner plate
cons: Smaller than the OptiChef Pro Max
Needs regular wiping to avoid smoke

buyingCriteria.explanation: Combos are microwaves before they are air fryers. The sweet spot for wattage is about 1000 to 1250 watts, and the 900 watt units, the Sharp and the BLACK+DECKER, run slower. The Toshiba OptiChef Pro Max at 1100 watts and the Panasonic at 1000 are closer to the target. Adjust package times if your wattage differs. A 900 watt microwave needs roughly a quarter more time than a 1200 watt one for the same load, and the gap widens on dense foods. Stir or turn halfway and rest the food for a minute, since cold spots are normal in any microwave.

buyingCriteria.criterion: How the air fry actually works
buyingCriteria.explanation: Combo air frying relies on a convection fan and a heating element, so it behaves more like a small convection oven than a basket. The Toshiba ChefFry Plus uses a top fan and element, and the Ninja uses FusionCrisp, which microwaves and then crisps. Expect a gentler result than a dedicated air fryer on thick frozen foods. The fan in a combo is sized for a cavity that also holds a turntable and a magnetron, so airflow is lower and the food sits farther from the element. Thin, flat items such as pizza slices and chicken tenders do best, while piles of fries stay softer.

Cubic feet is a weak guide, so look at the turntable diameter. A turntable of about 12.4 inches fits a standard dinner plate, as on the Toshiba 8-in-1. Compact 0.9 cubic foot cavities such as the Sharp suit single plates and small bowls. Check the interior height as well, because an air fry tray reduces the usable space and a tall dish may not fit under the top element. Measure the dishes you use most before you commit.

An inverter delivers continuous power rather than pulses, and the OptiChef Pro Max has one. A humidity sensor adjusts time to the steam off food. Both help with defrosting and gentle reheating, which is where microwaves often go wrong. Sensor cooking adjusts time by the steam leaving the food, so it works best on a covered dish of a typical portion. Do not expect it to rescue a very unusual load.

Convection plus microwave means grease and moisture both land in the cavity. Wipe after each use and clean the turntable. Never run the unit empty and use microwave-safe containers, since metal and foil can arc. A bowl of water with lemon heated for a few minutes loosens baked-on splatter, and a wipe afterwards finishes the job. Keep a dedicated cloth for the cavity, since grease on a shared sponge ends up everywhere.

Combos are larger and hotter than plain microwaves. Measure the space and leave ventilation clearance on all sides. A unit that cannot breathe overheats, and the first symptom is a convection cycle that ends early. A unit that cannot breathe overheats and cooks unevenly.

howWeEvaluated.title: Microwave performance first
howWeEvaluated.description: We treated each unit as a microwave before an air fryer and read wattage, cavity and turntable. The Toshiba lists 1100W and the Sharp 900W. Microwave quality sets the floor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Crisping approach
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how each combo crisps. Toshiba uses a top fan and element, Ninja uses FusionCrisp and the others use convection. None match a dedicated basket.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and guidance
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at screens, presets and app support. The Panasonic adds a recipe app and the BLACK+DECKER lists eleven air fry presets. Clear menus matter more in a combo.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety features
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted child locks and ventilation guidance. The Toshiba 8-in-1 lists a two-step child lock. Combos get hot, so clearance is essential. The outer shell can become very warm in air fry mode, so we favoured units that describe their cool-touch or ventilation design clearly. Households with young children should weigh that detail alongside the lock.

howWeEvaluated.title: Footprint and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared size and features against each tier. The Sharp is compact, and the Toshiba OptiChef is large. Listed prices move around, so value is a comparison of tiers here. We also considered how much cleaning each interior invites, since a combo with a top element and a fan collects splatter in more places than a plain box. Units that list a flat floor or a removable tray scored better on upkeep.

cards.label: Combo
cards.text: A combo saves counter space and adds multi-stage cooking. It crisps more gently than a basket, and it is heavier and hotter than a plain microwave.

cards.label: Separate
cards.text: A basket air fryer and a plain microwave cost two counter spots. Each does its job better, and either can be replaced alone.

howToChoose.note: Choose a combo for space and convenience, and separate machines for best performance.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a combo that fits your counter with ventilation clearance and a turntable that takes your plates. Do not trade away microwave power for the air fry label.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Toshiba OptiChef Pro Max is the best all-round combo. The Sharp suits small kitchens, and the Ninja suits crisp-first buyers.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want strong air frying or an inverter, which point to the Ninja and Toshiba OptiChef. A larger cavity and screen also justify a step up.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want the combo idea on a budget. The BLACK+DECKER or Sharp covers that at a low tier.

maintenance.why: Grease and moisture bake on under convection. A damp cloth removes it when cool.
Food residue causes odours and uneven turning. Wash it by hand.
A dirty seal can leak heat and microwaves. Wipe it and look for damage.
Blocked vents overheat the unit. Keep clearance on all sides.

Metal can arc in microwave mode. Check the manual for which accessories suit convection. Even in convection mode, the metal tray must not touch the cavity walls. Keep a note of which racks and trays are for which mode, since mixing them up is the usual cause of arcing.

faq.q: Is a microwave air fryer combo as good as a real air fryer?
faq.a: Not for crisping. A combo crisps more gently because the airflow is weaker than in a basket. That is a fair compromise when counter space is the priority.

faq.q: What wattage should I look for?
faq.a: About 1000 to 1250 watts is the sweet spot. The 900 watt models are slower and need longer times. Check package instructions against your wattage.

faq.q: Does air fry mode work in the microwave function?
faq.a: No. Air fry uses the convection fan and element, not the magnetron. Some units chain both automatically, as the Ninja FusionCrisp does.

faq.q: Can I use metal in the oven?
faq.a: Only in convection or air fry modes when the manual allows it. Never use metal or foil in microwave mode.
A child lock helps, and the Toshiba 8-in-1 lists a two-step lock. Surfaces get hot, so supervise children near the unit.

faq.q: How much space do I need?
faq.a: Measure the counter and leave ventilation clearance around the unit. Combos are larger and hotter than plain microwaves.
